Benjamin Netanyahu (1978): The Argument on Palestinian Statehood and Jordan🇵🇸🇯🇴 During a 1978 interview under the name Ben Nitay, 28-year-old Benjamin Netanyahu addressed whether Palestinians have a right to an independent state. Citing the Palestinian National Covenant's definition of Palestinians as part of the broader Arab nation, he noted that 21 Arab states already existed across vast territory and wealth. He argued that Jordan, with its majority-Palestinian population, effectively functioned as the Palestinian state, a characterization he pointed out was shared by both King Hussein and Yasser Arafat. From this perspective, he framed the establishment of another state not as a first homeland, but as the creation of a 22nd Arab nation and a second Palestinian state. #israel #palestine🇵🇸 #jordan #netanyahu #viralvideo

What Is Palestine? Palestine is a historical term for a region that has encompassed many territories — originally named by the Romans in 135 AD, when they renamed Judea in an attempt to sever the Jewish connection to the land. Across the centuries, the land was ruled by empire after empire, yet no sovereign country called Palestine ever existed. It began as a name meant to erase a people — and the question today is whether it's still being used to do exactly that. The last episode of "What Is" Season 1 is this Thursday at 11am ET.
